title: Join a book and its author
summary: A join combines records whose key values match.
introduction: A join combines records whose key values match. Your task: Add a second author and book to the sample.
learningObjectives: Add a second author and book to the sample.
Explain the example for join a book and its author

blocks.text: A join combines records whose key values match. It lets related facts stay in separate tables or query results.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.code:
WITH authors(id,name) AS (SELECT 1,'Mia' FROM dual), books(title,author_id) AS (SELECT 'Moon Trip',1 FROM dual)
SELECT b.title,a.name FROM books b JOIN authors a ON a.id=b.author_id;
blocks.title: Join a book and its author

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `DUAL` lets this Oracle statement return a calculation without an application table.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Moon Trip is paired with Mia.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Oracle table aliases in this syntax are written without AS. Keep dialect differences in mind.
